own_original_text:
An application having been duly made, pursuant to and in full compliance with the provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, for my approval of a Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry, and hearings having been held thereon and the Administrator having rendered his report containing an analysis of the said Code of Fair Competition together with his recommendations and findings with respect thereto, and the Administrator having found that the said Code of Fair Competition complies in all respects with the pertinent provisions of Title I of said Act and that the requirements of Clauses (1) and (2) of Subsection (a) of Section 3 of the said Act have been met:

Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do approve the report and recommendations and adopt the findings of the Administrator and do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

Approval Recommended:

     Hugh S Johnson

          Administrator.

The White House,

Jan. 31, 1934.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive order approving the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Applying the reviewed shared analysis: the code-dependent command had no own-terms end, no held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and Senate Joint Resolution 113 section 2 (June 14, 1935) repealed the code approval and enforcement provisions, so the approval ended on June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. The text is an American Presidency Project transcription held as a provisional working text under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; no certification is claimed.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no period, condition, \"until\" date, pending clause or provisional approval, and the lookup found no own-text signal. The held-corpus search found no cancellation, modification under section 10(b), superseding code, revocation or suspension of this code before June 14, 1935. Many held later orders name this code (supplementary subcodes and agreements approved under it, an order appointing a chairman of its planning and adjustment board, and Executive Order 6925 of December 19, 1934, which places the construction operations of the Cinders, Ashes, and Scavenger Trade under it); each acts under or extends the code, and none cancels, suspends, revokes or replaces the approval. The only number citation of 6578 in the held corpus is a Public Land Order, a different series. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935, so the first end is the statutory repeal; June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.","independent_command_check":"The order contains no appointment, committee, delegation, report direction or other command independent of the code; its other words are the recital of the application, hearings and the Administrator's findings, the signature and the Administrator's recommendation. The proviso to section 2 of the resolution names agreements and action thereunder and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed that exemption for past action under codes. No held source continues the approval after June 14, 1935 and no held source shows a prosecution under this code continued after that date; nothing here continues the approval itself.","scope_check":"Identity: the census register lists this order as 1934-01-31, Franklin D. The inventory is one clause, the sole operative paragraph that approves the code, which is complete; the held text was read in full. "}

savings_residuals.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry before June 14, 1935, and any fine, injunction or conviction already completed, are accrued effects that the repeal did not undo; the section 5 antitrust exemption for action already taken under an approved and effective code is likewise an accrued effect. The proviso to section 2 of the resolution names agreements and action thereunder and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed that exemption for past action under codes. No held source continues the approval after June 14, 1935 and no held source shows a prosecution under this code continued after that date; nothing here continues the approval itself.
